section.title: Paying for it
section.intro: Most of what this is supposed to cost can be reduced, covered, or dodged completely, and one route pays you instead. Every year people decline help they would have been given, because nobody sat them down and told them it was there.

items.title: HEAR
items.subtitle: Higher Education Access Route
items.summary: Gets you into college on fewer points than the person beside you, if your circumstances qualify. Most of the people it was built for never fill in the form.
items.body:
HEAR offers college places on reduced points, plus support once you are in, to school leavers from socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds. The universities run it through the CAO.

There is a genuine chance you qualify. It is assessed on your household, so you have to apply and show your circumstances rather than assume somebody has noticed them.

This is the most valuable thing on this website. People who would have qualified miss it every single year, and it is almost always one of three reasons: nobody mentioned it, the paperwork looked like a fortnight's work, or they decided in advance that it was meant for somebody worse off than them.

blocks.heading: What you actually get
blocks.text: A place at lower points than the published requirement, and support once you are there. Orientation, study help, in some cases money. It is not a lesser degree. Same course, same exams, same degree, and nobody can tell afterwards.

blocks.heading: The deadline is not the one you're thinking of
blocks.text: HEAR goes in with your CAO application, and the HEAR closing date lands well before the main one. Supporting documents have their own earlier date again. Miss it and you wait a year. Look up the current dates in the autumn of sixth year, not in the spring when somebody finally mentions it.

blocks.heading: There is paperwork and it is the real problem
blocks.text: Proof of income, evidence of your circumstances. None of it is hard. It's just boring, and boring is what stops people. Start early and put your guidance counsellor to work on it. This is exactly what they are there for and most of them will be glad to be asked.

blocks.heading: Applying costs you nothing
blocks.text: If it turns out you are not eligible, your ordinary CAO application carries on untouched. There is no version of this where applying makes you worse off.

myths.myth: It's for people in real hardship, not me.
myths.reality: It weighs several things together, not just income. Plenty of ordinary working households qualify. Let them decide rather than deciding for them.

myths.myth: Everyone will know I got in on reduced points.
myths.reality: They will not. It is not on your degree and nobody in your lectures is told.
You handle it. They help with documents. Nobody does it for you and nobody will chase you.

items.title: SUSI
items.subtitle: The grant
items.summary: Covers fees for a lot of students and pays maintenance to some. The commonest mistake is deciding you won't qualify and never finding out.
items.body:
SUSI is the national student grant. Depending on household income and circumstances it can cover the student contribution, and separately pay you a maintenance grant to live on.

The thresholds are higher than people guess. The application is free. Assuming you are above the line, without checking where the line is, is how students end up paying for something they would have got.

blocks.heading: Two separate things
blocks.text: One part covers your fees. The other pays you money for living on. They are assessed apart, so you might get one and not the other, and the maintenance grant pays more if college is far from home.

blocks.heading: Apply before you know where you're going
blocks.text: You do not need an offer in hand. Waiting until August means waiting for money you will need in September, at the exact moment everybody else is waiting too.

blocks.heading: It is not the only money in the building
blocks.text: Most colleges run a Student Assistance Fund for students hit by costs they did not see coming. Discretionary, confidential, and far quieter than it ought to be. Ask the access office in your first week, before you need it.

myths.reality: Possibly. The thresholds still surprise people and they move every year. Check rather than concluding.
There is a maintenance grant. It is paid to you.
